question: Who among the following social reformers wrote the book called ‘Barno-Porichoy’?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar:**

 
 
• In the nineteenth century, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, also called Ishwar Chandra Bandyopadhyay, was a well-known person in India.
 
• Born in West Bengal on September 26, 1820, Vidyasagar was** bestowed with the moniker Vidyasagar in 1839 due to his profound understanding of Sanskrit and philosophy.**
 
• Among other things, he studied Vedanta, Smruti, Astronomy, literature, dialectics, and Sanskrit grammar. 
 
• After passing the law exam in 1839, **Vidyasagar went on to earn his degree in 1841 from Sanskrit College in Kolkata.**
 
• As** Principal of Sanskrit College, Vidyasagar supervised enormous advancements in both administration and education between 1851 and 1858. **
 
• He felt that everyone should have access to education, regardless of gender or caste, and was a fervent advocate for universal education. 
 
• **At the age of 21, he was appointed head of Fort William College's Sanskrit department.** 
 
• **His efforts culminated in the Widow Remarriage Act being passed by the Indian government in 1856. **
 
• Along with fighting against child marriage, he established 35 schools for girls throughout Bengal.
 
• The first book given to a Bengali child is still **Vidyasagar's Borna Porichoy, which is an introduction to the alphabet.**
 
• Two of his books, **Upakaramonika and Byakaran Koumudi,** translated difficult topics from Sanskrit Grammar into Bengali.
 
• Among Vidyasagar's social reform writings are "Bahubivah," which condemned polygamy in 1871, "Bidhobabivah," which addresses the rights of widows to remarry in 1855, and "Balyabivah," which addresses the downsides of child marriage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Debendranath Tagore:**

 
 
• Debendranath Tagore (1817-1905) was born in Calcutta.
 
• He was a social reformer as well as a scholar.
 
• In 1842, he became a member of the Brahmo Samaj, which Raja Rammohan Roy had established in 1828.
 
• He **founded Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839, **and it began publishing a monthly theological journal called **Tattvabodhini Patrika in Bengali.**
 
• Tattvabodhini Sabha was eventually absorbed into the Bahmo Samaj.
 
• A **Tatwabodhini Pathshala, or Theological School, was founded in 1844 by Debendranath** with the purpose of teaching Vedanta and preparing young men to teach the Brahmo religion.
 
• Shortly after Keshab Chandra Sen's admission in samaj in 1858, he elevated Sen to the rank of acharya.
 
• **Keshab Chandra Sen and his followers established the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866** following his removal as acharya in 1865.
 
• **Debendranath Tagore's Samaj was later referred to as the Adi Brahmo Samaj.**
 
• The Brahma Dharma Grantha is a theistic textbook on religion and morality that he prepared and published.
 
 
 
• Swami Vivekananda:
 
 
• He was an Indian Hindu monk, philosopher, writer, and religious instructor.
 
• He lived from January 12, 1863, to July 4, 1902.
 
• Originally known as Narendranath Datta.
 
• He was the foremost pupil of the saint Ramakrishna from India.
 
• He had a significant role in bringing yoga and Vedanta to the West.
 
• He is recognised as the founder of contemporary Indian nationalism and for having elevated interfaith understanding and elevated Hinduism to the level of a significant global religion.
 
• He established the Vedanta Society of San Francisco (now known as the Vedanta Society of Northern California) and the Vedanta Society of New York, which served as the models for other Vedanta Societies in the West.
 
• In September 1893, he delivered his well-known speech at the "Parliament of Religions" convention in Chicago.
 
• In 1897, he made his way back to Inida.
 
• In India, Vivekananda established the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897, which offers social work, education, and charitable services, as well as the Ramakrishna Math, which trains monastics and lay followers in spirituality.
 
 
 
• **Dwarkanath Ganguly:**
 
 
• He was a Brahmo reformer who was born on 20 April 1844 and deid on 27 June 1898.
 
• He was also known as Dwarkanath Gangopadhyay.
 
• He made a significant contribution to women's freedom and societal enlightenment.
 
• He was** the spouse of Kadambini Ganguly, the first Indian woman physician.**
 
• **He published the periodical Abalabandhab (Friend of Women) in Dhaka in May 1869. **
 
• **Sanjivani, a weekly Bengali newspaper that aimed to unite the peasants of lower Bengal, was published by him and Krishna Kumar Mitra.**
 
• Ganguly held multiple terms as the** secretary of the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj, which was established by Umeshchandra Datta, Shibchandra Deb, and Ananda Mohan Bose.**
